test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 2 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Who among the following Mughal rulers of India gave permission to the British to establish their first factory in Surat?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jahangir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nur-ud-Din Muhammad Salim**, known by his **imperial name Jahangir**.
 
• He was the **fourth Mughal Emperor**.
 
• He **ruled **from **1605 **until **his death in 1627**.
 
• He was **born on 30 August 1569 **in **Fatehpur Sikri **and **died **on **28 October 1627 **in **Rajouri**.
 
• He is **famous **for his **'golden chain of justice**.
 
• A **golden chain **having **60 bells **and **weighing several 'maunds**' was fastened between the **Shahburj of Agra fort **and a **stone pillar raised on the banks of river Jamuna**.
 
• He was the **Mughal ruler **of **India **who gave **permission to the British **to **establish their first factory in Surat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shah Jahan**, Mughal emperor **from 1628 to 1658**, is perhaps **best remembered **for the **grand monuments **constructed during his reign, especially the **Taj Mahal **and the **Motī Masjid (Pearl Mosque**) in **Agra **and the **Jāmiʿ Masjid **and **Red Fort in Delhi**.
 
• **Bahadur Shah Zafar **was a noted **Urdu poet**, having written a **number of Urdu ghazals**. While some part of his **opus was lost or destroyed during the Indian Rebellion **of **1857**, a large collection did **survive **and was **compiled **into the **Kulliyyat-i-Zafar**.
 
• **Aurangzeb **is known for being the **emperor of India from 1658 to 1707**. He was the **last of the great Mughal emperors**. Under him the **Mughal Empire **reached its **greatest extent**, although his **policies helped lead to its dissolution.**
